Configurations: RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; a `template_release` export; Forward+/Vulkan (the ADR-0008 pin) and the step-9 Compatibility branch; pass A, plus pass B if built; the shipped `shadow_filter` and NONE; Direct3D 12 only if the ADR-0008 tie-break calls for it.
210	
211	**8.2 The probe pack (committed, windowed, rerun on every engine patch bump and driver-pin change).** `tests/integration/lighting/shadow_origin_probe_pack/` rebuilds the scenes above with the **shipping** `OccluderSource`, occluder builder and EM-20 segment function (not re-implementations), writes the counts and the retained captures to `production/qa/evidence/`, and fails on a stated bound. It is a manual/windowed gate (a headless CI run cannot draw; the Compatibility fallback must not be mistaken for the pinned renderer, ADR-0008's headless-tier finding).
212	
213	| Probe | Question | Pass |
214	|---|---|---|
215	| SO-P1 | Does the shadow origin follow the node and ignore `offset` and `rotation`? | dark runs identical in the three P-1 cases |
216	| SO-P2 | `offset` frame (LOCAL/WORLD) and whether it is scaled by `texture_scale` | LOCAL, unscaled (any other result is an amendment, § 4.2) |
217	| SO-P3 | Apex centroid for five angles with the real edge-apex textures (LO-15) | within 0.01 px of `render(foot) + v` |
218	| SO-P4 | A light inside a closed polygon, each `cull_mode` | recorded; `CULL_DISABLED` is the shipped mode |
219	| SO-P5 | Fractional position honoured, snap flags (pass A and pass B) | recorded; B requires honoured and unsnapped |
220	| SO-P6 | Lattice scenes (P-7, P-8) | zero mismatches at radius 2 with the lattice; radius 1 recorded |
221	| SO-P7 | The AC-57 matrix: 5 values of s x 4 aims x 7 `CHEST_POINT` rows = **140 rows** per configuration, one table row each, pass or recorded failure | zero radius-2 mismatches, zero black beams, per row |
222	| SO-P8 | `shadow_filter` NONE / PCF5 / PCF13 | the shipped level keeps radius 2 at zero; the radius-1 count is recorded and sets the stated agreement |
223	| SO-P9 | Pass B at the built ladder rungs (k = 2, 3 probed) and a merged multi-vertex polygon | zero radius-2 mismatches |
224	
225	**8.3 The result is recorded by amendment.** `## Spike Result` is appended with: the rung that passed and the reason each earlier rung did not; the table of SO-P1 to SO-P9 per configuration; the measured `OFFSET_FRAME`; the `shadow_filter` chosen; the radius-1 and radius-2 counts; links to the retained captures (`production/qa/evidence/em-shadow-origin-[s]-[aim]-[date].png` as AC-57 names them, and the pack's log). Status moves to Accepted only with that section and only after the GDD syncs (§ Related) are applied. A rung D result also amends ADR-0017.
226	
227	### Key Interfaces
228	
229	```gdscript
230	# src/presentation/pipeline/placement.gd      CELL_CENTRE, put_light_origin   (shown in § 3.1; ADR-0009 § 4 host)
231	# src/presentation/lighting/beam_offset.gd    BeamOffset.offset_for            (shown in § 4.2; pure)
232	
233	# src/presentation/lighting/shadow_origin.gd   (pure; the contract of § 2 as a testable function)
234	class_name ShadowOrigin extends RefCounted
235	enum Mode { FOOT_OFFSET = 0, CHEST_NODE = 1, OCC_PUBLISHED = 2 }
236	## The render-frame point the engine will cast shadows from, for the simulation's integer occlusion origin p. SO-1.
237	static func render_origin(p: Vector2i) -> Vector2:
238		return Vector2(p) + Placement.CELL_CENTRE
239	
240	# tests/integration/lighting/shadow_origin_probe_pack/boundary_metric.gd   (test-only; § 2 SO-2)
241	## Count of cells where sim_lit and drawn_lit differ and every cell within Chebyshev distance `radius` has the same simulation answer.
242	static func mismatches_at_radius(sim: PackedByteArray, drawn: PackedByteArray, w: int, h: int, radius: int) -> int
243	```
244	
245	Data (no values restated; cite names): `LightingTuning.SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE`, `OCC_MARGIN_PX`, `SHADOW_ATLAS_PX`, `OFFSET_FRAME` (LOCAL, fixed by P-2), `OCCLUDER_VERTS_MAX`; Emitter: reserved `OCC_ORIGIN_MODE`; Body: `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`; Controller: the chest offset (`CHEST_POINT[sheet][anim]` mirrored, registry `chest_point`).
246	
247	### Implementation Guidelines
248	
249	- **Must** position every `Light2D` through `Placement.put_light_origin` and no other path; **must never** write a shadow-casting light's `position` with `Placement.put`, `position =`, `global_position =` or any relative-move call (lint SHO-01, PRES-03).
250	- **Must** write `Light2D.offset` of a hard-shaped light every render frame, write-on-change, from `BeamOffset.offset_for` with the rotation read back from the same node, in stage LIGHTING; **must never** write it from the Presenter or from a cached rotation (SHO-02, SHO-03).
251	- **Must** keep the beam node's parent non-rotating and **must never** parent a `Light2D` to the avatar, the tool layer or any node that rotates (LO-2).
252	- **Must** build occluder polygons from the integer corners of `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangles with `CULL_DISABLED` and no shift; **must never** use `CULL_CLOCKWISE` or `CULL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE` (P-4, P-9), a `TileSet` occluder layer, or a polygon vertex off the integer lattice.
253	- **Must** measure the shadow-reach occluder set from the apex (§ 4.4); **must never** measure it from the node.
254	- **Must** read the foot from `body.state` (`pos_x`, `pos_y`, `prev_x`, `prev_y`, ADR-0015 § 11.3) under B and **must never** read `controller.state` for the origin; the chest offset is the only Controller read.
255	- **Must** select the mode from `LightingTuning.SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE` once at setup; **must never** branch on it per frame inside a hot loop (a strategy chosen at `setup()`), and **must** fail boot on an illegal pair (`LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO`).
256	- **Must not** add a second shadow-casting light per beam (C), a physics query, or a renderer-to-simulation feedback of any kind (TR-light-002).
257	- **Must** rerun the probe pack of § 8.2 when the engine patch version, the renderer method, the driver pin or `shadow_filter` changes, and keep its log in `production/qa/evidence/`.
258	
259	## Alternatives Considered
260	
261	### Alternative 1: Fold the decision into ADR-0028
262	- **Description**: ADR-0028 (2D lighting budget and modifier chain) carries the shadow origin as one section, as the architecture note allows if the spike settles both at once.
263	- **Pros**: one fewer ADR; the Lighting-side detail lives with the rest of Lighting.

# Godot — Breaking Changes

Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.6 → 4.7 and the section dates); 2026-02-12 (older sections)

Changes between Godot versions, focused on post-LLM-cutoff changes (4.4+).

## 4.6 → 4.7 (Jun 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)

From the official migration guide
(https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html,
checked 2026-10-17). Rows marked **GDScript breaks** stop existing GDScript from
working; the rest add optional parameters, change C# compatibility only, or
change behaviour or defaults. The guide lists no deprecations.

| Subsystem | Change | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| GDScript | Overrides inherit a typed return | An override of a method with a typed return now inherits that type, so it needs an explicit `return` (add `return null` to fix the error). **GDScript breaks** |
| GDScript | Packed array element writes | Setting one element of a packed array no longer calls the setter of the whole packed-array property |
| GUI | `RichTextLabel.ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_IN_PERCENT` renamed | Now `UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT`. **GDScript breaks** |
| GUI | `RichTextLabel.add_image()` / `update_image()` | `width` / `height` are `float` (were `int`); `width_in_percent` / `height_in_percent` renamed `width_unit` / `height_unit`, typed `RichTextLabel.ImageUnit` (were `bool`, default `false` → `0`). C# source breaks |
| GUI | `Control.accessibility_live` type | `AccessibilityServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` (was `DisplayServer.AccessibilityLiveMode`). C# breaks |
| Core | `Object.is_class()` | Parameter is `StringName` (was `String`) |
| Core | `OptimizedTranslation.generate()` | Returns `bool` (was `void`). C# binary breaks |
| Input | Mouse and keyboard device IDs | Were `0`; now `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` and `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`, because some joypads use `0`. Identify events by type or compare `InputEvent.device` to those constants |
| Physics | Jolt: `WorldBoundaryShape3D` plane sign | The sign of `plane.d` is read the way Godot Physics reads it, so it is flipped compared to 4.6: negate it to keep 4.6 behaviour |
| Physics | Jolt: `SoftBody3D` mass and stiffness | Mass defaults to 1 kg for the whole body (was 1 kg per point); `linear_stiffness` is applied differently. Re-tune `linear_stiffness` and `damping_coefficient` on every `SoftBody3D` |
| Physics | Jolt: `Area3D` and `SoftBody3D` | `Area3D` now reports overlaps with `SoftBody3D`; use collision layers and masks to ignore them |
| Physics | `PhysicsServer2D.body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` | Optional `direction` added; `PhysicsServer2DExtension._body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` requires it (extensions break) |
| Audio | `AudioStreamPlayer2D` / `AudioStreamPlayer3D` `area_mask` default | Changed from layer `1` to `0` (disabled). An `Area2D`/`Area3D` `audio_bus_override` that relied on the default mask stops working until the mask is set back to layer `1` |
| Audio | `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.tap_back_pos` | Removed. **GDScript breaks** where it is used |
| Rendering | `CanvasItem` line drawing | No antialiasing feather is added, so lines look thinner; widen lines that relied on the old thickness |
| Rendering | `LinearToSRGB` visual shader node | No longer clamps to `[0.0, 1.0]` under Forward+ and Mobile |
| Rendering | `get_format()` moved | From `ImageTexture` / `PortableCompressedTexture2D` to base class `Texture2D` |
| Rendering | `RenderingServer.particles_request_process_time()` | `time` renamed `process_time`; optional `process_time_residual` added (also on `request_particles_process()` of the four particle nodes) |
| Rendering | Sky reflection roughness layers | `rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers` default `7` → `8` |
| Animation | `Animation.length` | Type metadata `double` (was `float`). C# breaks |
| Animation | `LookAtModifier3D.relative` | Default `false` (was `true`) |
| Animation | `AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D/2D.add_blend_point()` | Optional `name` added |
| Project | Stretch defaults for NEW projects | `display/window/stretch/mode` `canvas_items` (was `disabled`), `display/window/stretch/aspect` `expand` (was `keep`). Existing projects keep their settings |
| Text | `ResourceImporterDynamicFont.hinting` | Default `3` (was `1`) |
| Editor | `EditorSceneFormatImporter` import constants | Moved into the `ImportFlags` enum (`IMPORT_SCENE`, `IMPORT_ANIMATION`, …). C# source breaks |
| Editor | `EditorVCSInterface._commit()` | New `amend` parameter; VCS plugins break |
| Editor | Asset Library replaced by the Asset Store | The editor workspace is now "Asset Store" (release notes: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/) |
| XR | `OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_register_metadata()` | New `interaction_profile_metadata` parameter; extensions break |

## 4.5 → 4.6 (Jan 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)

| Subsystem | Change | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Physics | Jolt is now the DEFAULT 3D physics engine | New projects use Jolt automatically. Existing projects keep their setting. Some HingeJoint3D properties (like `damp`) only work with GodotPhysics. |
| Rendering | Glow processes BEFORE tonemapping | Was after tonemapping. Scenes with glow will look different. Adjust intensity/blend in WorldEnvironment. |
| Rendering | D3D12 default on Windows | Was Vulkan. For better driver compatibility. **Correction, 2026-10-29:** on 4.7.2 `ProjectSettings.get_setting("rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows")` returns `vulkan` for a project (probed 2026-10-28); the D3D12-default claim is unverified for projects (a 4.7.2 project with no driver key reports vulkan, and the ProjectSettings default of `driver.wind
| Rendering | AgX tonemapper new controls | White point and contrast parameters added. |
| Core | Quaternion initializes to identity | Was zero. Unlikely to affect most code but technically breaking. |
| UI | Dual-focus system | Mouse/touch focus now separate from keyboard/gamepad focus. Visual feedback differs by input method. |
| Animation | IK system fully restored | CCDIK, FABRIK, Jacobian IK, Spline IK, TwoBoneIK via SkeletonModifier3D nodes. |
| Editor | New "Modern" theme default | Grayscale replaces blue-tint. Restore: Editor Settings → Interface → Theme → Style: Classic |
| Editor | "Select Mode" keybind changed | New "Select Mode" (v key) prevents accidental transforms. Old mode renamed "Transform Mode" (q key). |
| 2D | TileMapLayer scene tile rotation | Scene tiles can now be rotated like atlas tiles. |
| Localization | CSV plural form support | No longer requires Gettext for plurals. Context columns added. |
----
1:# Godot Rendering — Quick Reference

14:- **`rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers`** default `7` → `8` (4.7 migration guide: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html)
17:- **D3D12 is the default rendering backend on Windows** (was Vulkan) per the 4.6 migration notes; the installed 4.7.2 editor was probed 2026-10-28 reporting `rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = vulkan` as its built-in default, so pin and assert the driver explicitly (ADR-0008 s1) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0008 sync)*
30:- **`RenderingDevice.draw_list_begin`**: Many parameters removed; optional `breadcrumb` added
32:  `get_default_texture_parameter()` returns `Texture`, not `Texture2D` (the shading

56:### Rendering Backend Selection (4.6)

63:Windows default backend: D3D12 (was Vulkan pre-4.6) per the 4.6 migration notes; NOTE probed 2026-10-28: the installed 4.7.2 editor reports rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows = vulkan as its built-in default, so pin and assert the driver explicitly (ADR-0008 s1)
70:- Passing or expecting `Texture2D` in `Shader.set_default_texture_parameter()` /
72:  language's `sampler2D` / `texture()` did not change)

309	## Consequences
310	
311	### Positive
312	- The spike is mechanical: a ladder, nine probes and one table, with the answer pre-registered and the probes already shown to pass for B on one machine.
313	- The simulation does not change under B. The only presentation change is one `Placement` function, one lint allow-list entry and one sweep exemption.
314	- One lattice rule covers every light, and it removes the polygon-face degeneracy by parity.
315	- D is specified and cheap: the Presenter already takes its origin from a named source.
316	- The interface unblocks the Avatar Presenter and Lighting stories before ADR-0028 exists.
317	
318	### Negative
319	- A fractional `Light2D.position` is a deliberate exception to "every written position has a zero fractional part" (ADR-0009 § 4), which needs Foundation sign-off (F1) and a second lint rule (SHO-03 lattice check) beside the integral sweep.
320	- B has an ordering dependency (AVATAR before LIGHTING) that A would not; it is satisfied by an existing stage order, but a future change to the stage list must preserve it (SHO-03 catches a violation every frame in dev builds).
321	- B keeps a two-origin model on screen: a cone drawn from the chest with shadows cast from the feet. It is the same model the simulation uses, so they agree, but a wall footprint that lies between the chest and the foot can shade a region the chest alone would light. Whether that reads naturally is UNVERIFIED (playtest).
322	- All pre-spike evidence is from one machine and an editor build.
323	
324	## Risks
325	- **R1: the release export or the reference GPUs behave differently from the dev machine** (shadow origin from `offset`, the frame, the lattice response). *Mitigation*: the probe pack is the gate; A and D are specified; nothing is Accepted without it.
326	- **R2: the viewport snap flags round light positions on a path not probed** (the probe covered pass A with the flags on the `SubViewport`, not the root or pass B with a non-integer stretch). *Mitigation*: SO-P5 runs both passes; if snapping rounds lights, `put_light_origin` is replaced by a node-parent offset (an amendment) or the flags are turned off for the light parent.
327	- **R3: merged multi-vertex polygons and real edge-apex textures behave differently from the one-rectangle, centred-texture probes.** *Mitigation*: SO-P3 and SO-P9 use the shipping builder and textures; failure stops Acceptance.
328	- **R4: `shadow_filter` PCF widens the disagreement beyond radius 1.** *Mitigation*: SO-P8 sets the shipped level; the agreement statement is then the measured one, and a PCF level that breaks radius 2 is not shipped.
329	- **R5: the half-cell exception spreads** (other presenters copy it). *Mitigation*: `put_light_origin` takes a `Light2D`, not a `Node2D`; SHO-01 bans the pattern elsewhere.
330	- **R6: a later change to the occluder polygon builder shifts vertices or changes the cull mode.** *Mitigation*: SHO-05 and SHO-06 (cull mode and vertex lattice) and the probe pack rerun.
331	- **R7: ADR-0017 publishes `occ_origin` differently from what § 7 assumes.** *Mitigation*: listed under Cross-ADR assumptions; the identity contract only needs one published integer pair per beam.
332	- **R8: the prediction that A fails is wrong on the reference machines.** *Mitigation*: A is run as a control; if it passes every AC-57 row B still passes first by the ladder, so nothing is lost.
333	
334	## GDD Requirements Addressed
335	
336	### Decided here (1)
337	
338	| GDD System | Requirement | How This ADR Addresses It |
339	|------------|-------------|--------------------------|
340	| 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md | **TR-light-015**: Shadow origin must match the simulation's segment origin (foot, via `body.state` pos_curr / `occ_origin`) versus chest apex, with a spike-decided mechanism (preference B, A, D; C rejected) (LO-10; Emitter EM-6, AC-57, AC-LO-15, candidate 5) | § 2 fixes the identity contract and its measure; § 3 the lattice rule that makes it exact; § 4 the beam mechanism under B; § 5 the ladder and selection rule; § 6 the data switch; § 7 the contingency D; § 8 the spike, probe pack and gate. **Covered as a decision; the rung is pending spike step 3b** (B is the design of record, A is predicted to fail by P-9). |
341	
342	### Owned elsewhere (loaded or checked here only)
343	
344	| GDD System | Requirement | Where it is decided |
345	|------------|-------------|---------------------|
346	| emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query.md | **TR-emitter-016**: Beam geometry: apex/reach from `chest_sim`, axis from committed aim, occlusion segment starts at the foot origin (`pos_curr`); shape table; rendered reach equals table reach +/- 1 px | ADR-0017 (this ADR reads `occ_origin` and the chest offset and assumes they are separate fields; § 7 is the amendment path) |
347	| pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md | **TR-pxl-005**: every node placed at integer base px by one floor function, incl. the beam chest point | ADR-0009 § 4 (this ADR adds one function and one constant to it: Foundation ask F1) |
348	| player-controller-input.md | **TR-pc-026**, **TR-pc-040**: the Presenter writes only `Light2D` `position`/`rotation`; its pose write precedes Lighting's apply in the same render callback | ADR-0019 § 7 and ADR-0009 § 3 (this ADR gives the position write its meaning: foot + `CELL_CENTRE` under B) |
349	| player-controller-input.md | **TR-pc-041**: `emitter.place` reads the beam origin from `chest_sim`; Presenter light origin, rotation and sprite position unchanged by a Filter substitution | ADR-0024 (not this ADR; § 4.1 reads the origin from `body.state`, which a rig substitution does not change) |
350	| 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md | **TR-light-006**: Lighting and the Presenter own disjoint `Light2D` member sets, Presenter before Lighting | ADR-0028 (the disjointness lint is theirs; § 4.1 depends on it) |
351	| 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md | **TR-light-014**, **TR-light-035**: the occluder builder builds `LightOccluder2D` from `OccluderSource` rects; only `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rects occlude; no TileSet layer | ADR-0014 and ADR-0028 (§ 3.3 and § 4.4 constrain how the polygons are placed and which set is built, not how it is built) |
352	| 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md | **TR-light-019**: zoom by logical size; all `Light2D` lengths in base px | ADR-0008 § 3.1 (P-11 checks the lattice at k = 2, 3 under an override) |
353	| 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md | **TR-light-040**: unverified engine capabilities (including the light-texture `offset`) probed in the lighting spike and read back at startup | ADR-0028 (§ 8 supplies the `offset` and shadow-origin probes; a startup read-back of a drawn property is not possible headless, so the probe pack is the guard) |
354	| ship-body-and-interior-physics.md | **TR-shipbody-029**, **TR-shipbody-043**: `body.state` read view readable by PRESENTATION; Emitter and Lighting anchor on floored `pos_curr` | ADR-0015 § 11.3 (this ADR reads `pos_x`, `pos_y`, `prev_x`, `prev_y`) |
355	
356	## Performance Implications
357	- **CPU**: negligible. Per render frame one `Vector2.rotated` and one subtraction per hard-shaped light in view, write-on-change, no allocation (`Vector2` is a value type). `put_light_origin` is a compare and an assignment. Outcome D (contingency) adds a bounded integer scan of at most about 45 cells per beam per tick inside `emitter.place`, charged to ADR-0017's work-unit budget.
358	- **Memory**: none; no new nodes, no new state, no new persisted data.
359	- **Load Time**: none. One boot invariant (`LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO`) over two scalar rows.
360	- **GPU**: unchanged: the shadow-casting light count and the occluder set are the same under B as under A; the origin does not change the cost of a shadow pass (UNVERIFIED; measured by spike step 3).
361	- **Network**: none.
362	
363	## Migration Plan
364	No code exists. The order of work: (1) ADR-0009 gains `Placement.CELL_CENTRE` and `put_light_origin`, the two allow-list entries and the sweep exemption (F1, F2); (2) ADR-0019's Presenter story writes the beam node through `put_light_origin` from `body.state`; (3) the Lighting epic writes `BeamOffset` and the offset writer and commits the probe pack; (4) the Sprint-0 lighting spike runs step 3b on the reference machines and appends `## Spike Result`; (5) GDD syncs applied and Status moved to Accepted. If the spike selects D, ADR-0017 is amended first and (2) reads the published pair.
365

```gdscript
# src/presentation/pipeline/placement.gd
class_name Placement extends RefCounted
## Interpolate previous to current at alpha, then floor, per axis. alpha is clamped by the caller's PresentFrame.
static func at(prev: Vector2i, curr: Vector2i, alpha: float) -> Vector2i:
	return Vector2i(floori(prev.x + (curr.x - prev.x) * alpha), floori(prev.y + (curr.y - prev.y) * alpha))

## Alpha for a block whose owner runs every n ticks and publishes the tick it last ran (Horror alpha_5, PR-9).
static func alpha_n(run_tick: int, T: int, alpha: float, n: int) -> float:
	return clampf((float(T - run_tick) + alpha) / float(n), 0.0, 1.0)

## Floor a float vector to whole pixels, per axis. The integer helper for derived offsets that are not a prev/curr pair
## (the camera host's parallax layer offsets are built from this, never from a bare floor(); ADR-0008 § 6.2).
static func floor_v(v: Vector2) -> Vector2i:
	return Vector2i(floori(v.x), floori(v.y))

## The only assignment point for a Node2D position in presentation. Skips an unchanged write.
static func put(node: Node2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
	var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
	if node.position != v:
		node.position = v

## The same for a Control: HUD plates that follow world things (layer 2) are Controls (ADR-0008 § 5.5), and Control has no Node2D.position.
static func put_control(c: Control, p: Vector2i) -> void:
	var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
	if c.position != v:
		c.position = v
```

No deprecated or post-cutoff API is used, and none of the 4.7 hazards you listed (typed-return override, packed-array element-write setters, Object-method name clashes, const of a constructed object) occurs. findings.text: `offset` is not a `Light2D` property. Probed on 4.7.2: Light2D's own properties are enabled, editor_only, color, energy, blend_mode, range_*, shadow_enabled, shadow_color, shadow_filter, shadow_filter_smooth and shadow_item_cull_mask. `texture`, `offset`, `texture_scale` and `height` belong to `PointLight2D`; `DirectionalLight2D` has only `height` and `max_distance`. The ADR says 'Light2D.offset' throughout (Summary, § 1(b), SHO-02, F2 'a Light2D offset', the 'every hard-shaped light' rule). An offset writer typed `Light2D` will not parse the property statically and fails at run time on the abstract type. `put_light_origin(node: Light2D, ...)` is fine, because it uses only `position`, and the snippet compiled and ran (pos 10.5, -2.5).
findings.amendment: Say 'PointLight2D.offset' everywhere. Type `beam_offset_writer.gd` parameters as `PointLight2D`. State that every hard-shaped (textured) light is a PointLight2D and a DirectionalLight2D never goes through `BeamOffset`. Keep `put_light_origin(node: Light2D, ...)` as written; it is valid because it only touches `position`.

findings.text: Untested engine behaviour that could break rung B: culling of occluders by the light's texture-quad extent. The ADR itself leaves this open (OQ-E, § 4.4). My recollection of the 4.x canvas renderer is that occluders are attached to a light only if their AABB intersects the light's quad (rect_cache, which includes `offset` and `texture_scale`). I could not verify this headless. State in ADR-0008 that snapping applies to CanvasItem draw transforms and was probed not to apply to Light2D positions.

findings.text: Engine gotchas not stated: (a) `LightOccluder2D.sdf_collision` defaults to true (probed), which makes pooled occluders SDF contributors; set false unless something samples the SDF (cost UNVERIFIED). (b) `Light2D.shadow_item_cull_mask` and `LightOccluder2D.occluder_light_mask` both default to 1; the occluder builder and every shadow-casting light should set them explicitly so a later layer change cannot silently drop shadows. (c) `Light2D.shadow_filter_smooth` exists alongside `shadow_filter`, and SO-P8 only varies the enum, so PCF results are incomplete. (d) shadow resolution is bounded by `rendering/2d/shadow_atlas/size`, shared across shadow lights; the ADR names `SHADOW_ATLAS_PX` but SO-P6 does not require recording it.
findings.amendment: Add to § 3.3 / SHO-05: occluder pool nodes set `sdf_collision = false`, `occluder_light_mask` and the light's `shadow_item_cull_mask` explicitly. Extend SO-P8 to record `shadow_filter_smooth` and the atlas size with each count.

findings.text: Verified headless on 4.7.2 (no finding against the ADR): `const CELL_CENTRE: Vector2 = Vector2(0.5, 0.5)` compiles (a builtin value type, not a constructed Object); `static func` bodies of Placement.put_light_origin, BeamOffset.offset_for and ShadowOrigin.render_origin compile and run; `enum Mode {..}` is fine; `Vector2(Vector2i)` is exact; `x + 0.5` is exactly representable in float32 at 8388607 (so the 2^23 bound and WORLD_COORD_LIMIT 4194304 = 2^22 with a factor of two to spare are correct); `OccluderPolygon2D.CULL_DISABLED/CLOCKWISE/COUNTER_CLOCKWISE` and `Light2D.SHADOW_FILTER_NONE/PCF5/PCF13` exist with the names used; `SubViewport.size_2d_override_stretch`, `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` exist (defaults false). The PackedByteArray parameters of `mismatches_at_radius` are read-only, so by-reference passing and the 4.7 element-write change do not matter. There are no overrides, so the typed-return rule is not triggered, and no parameter is named get/set/free/call. Display note: `print(Vector2)` rounds large values (8388607.5 prints as 8388608); use `%.1f` or `is_equal_approx` in test output.
findings.amendment: None required. Keep test assertions on exact float equality, not on printed text.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0018 (header, § 6, § 7 and the Cross-ADR assumptions) assumes ADR-0017 publishes a `beam_pose.occ_origin` field and reserves a tuning key `OCC_ORIGIN_MODE`, and says ADR-0017 is not on disk. It has one function, `EmitterDerived.occlusion_origin(row, out_xy)` (D5.3), no `OCC_ORIGIN_MODE` (0 occurrences), and one occurrence of the string occ_origin (in its Enables row). The § 6 boot invariant over the pair (OCC_ORIGIN_MODE, SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE) cannot be evaluated as written.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0019 § 7.2 says the Presenter writes 'the integer `position` (through `Placement.put` only)' and also 'the chest `Light2D`'s `position`', without saying which function or which point. ADR-0018 requires `Placement.put_light_origin` with foot + (0.5, 0.5) for the Light2D, and a chest point is never the node position under B. `Placement.put(node: Node2D, p: Vector2i)` accepts a Light2D (it is a Node2D) and would write the integer foot; nothing in GDScript typing prevents the wrong call, only lint SHO-01.

ADR-0018 F1/F2 require a `light_origin` group exemption asserting a 0.5 lattice (bound 2^23) plus a PRES-03 allow-list entry for the PointLight2D `offset` writer.
